tools.name: help-center-search-articles
tools.description: Searches published help center articles and returns the best matches with a short summary. Use it before answering any customer question. Pass one to three keywords (for example "refund" or "reset password"), not a whole sentence: an article only matches if it contains every keyword. Then read the most relevant article in full with help-center-get-article.

query.description: One to three keywords, e.g. "refund" or "reset password".

topic.description: Optional topic slug to narrow the search, e.g. "billing". help-center-list-topics returns the valid slugs.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Defaults to 5.

tools.title: Search help articles

hint.description: What to try next when nothing matched.

tools.name: help-center-get-article
tools.description: Returns the full text of one help article by ID (IDs come from help-center-search-articles). Link the article URL when you use it in an answer.

tools.name: help-center-list-topics
tools.description: Lists the help center topics with their slugs and how many published articles each one has. Use it to see what the help center covers, or to find a valid topic slug for help-center-search-articles or help-center-create-draft.
tools.title: List help topics

tools.name: help-center-create-draft
tools.description: Saves a new help article as a draft for a human editor to review. It is never published automatically. Use it only when the help center does not already cover a question, and read the help-center://style-guide resource first. Write plain text: a blank line between paragraphs, "## " to start a heading, "- " to start a list item. Mark any fact you are not sure about as [CHECK: ...] so the editor verifies it.

title.description: The question as a customer would ask it, e.g. "How do I cancel my order?".

summary.description: One-sentence answer, shown in search results.

content.description: The article body as plain text, using the formatting rules above.

structuredContent.summary: One of the charges is usually a temporary authorization hold that your bank removes within 3-5 business days.
structuredContent.content:
If you see two charges for one order, one of them is almost always a temporary authorization hold. Your bank places the hold when you order and removes it automatically, usually within 3-5 business days.

Only the charge made when your order ships is final.

If both charges are still there after 5 business days, contact us with your order number and we will refund the duplicate.

steps.text:
One of the two charges is almost certainly a temporary authorization hold, not a second payment. Your bank places the hold when you order and removes it automatically, usually within 3-5 business days. Only the charge made when your order ships is final.

If both charges are still there after 5 business days, contact us with your order number and we'll refund the duplicate.

Source: [Why was I charged twice?](http://localhost:8888/help/charged-twice/)

contents.text:
# Fernhill help center style guide

- **Audience:** customers, not engineers. Use plain language and address the reader as "you".
- **Title:** the question as a customer would ask it, e.g. "How do I reset my password?".
- **Structure:** answer in the first sentence, then the steps as a list, then edge cases.
- **Length:** under 250 words, one question per article.
- **Facts:** never invent policies, prices, dates or deadlines. Mark anything unconfirmed as [CHECK: ...] so the editor verifies it.
- **Ending:** stop after the last fact. Don't add a contact line: every article page already ends with a "Contact support" box.

arguments.title: Can I cancel my order after placing it?
arguments.summary: You can cancel an order until it ships [CHECK: confirm this policy]. Your card is only charged when the order ships.
arguments.content:
You can cancel an order as long as it hasn't shipped yet. [CHECK: confirm that orders can be cancelled until they ship.]

- Sign in and open Account > Orders.
- Choose the order and select "Cancel order". [CHECK: confirm this option exists and what it is called.]
- Confirm the cancellation. We email you when it's done.

Your card is only charged when your order ships, so a cancelled order is never charged. If your bank shows a temporary authorization hold, it disappears within 3-5 business days.

Already shipped? You can't cancel it anymore, but you can return unused items within 30 days of delivery.
